cohort: 74 women who had undergone primary repair of a fourth-degree OASIS
finding: The majority of women with a history of fourth-degree OASIS have sphincter defects and abnormal anal manometry findings, even if asymptomatic, suggesting that cesarean section may be a reasonable option for subsequent deliveries.
mod_finding: Caesarean section is recommended for all women with a history of fourth-degree OASIS, especially in the absence of specialist investigations like endoanal ultrasound and anal manometry.
